body:
Florida is 2-0 because two Saturdays never got close. That is the whole of it, and the limit of it. Saturday at Auburn is the first night a game can stay close long enough for a slow start and a pile of flags to decide it.

Jon Sumrall had 66 on Florida Atlantic, Aaron Philo 16-of-21, and still spent Monday on a corner sitting nine yards off the ball on 3rd-and-short, on a defense that took the deep ball and let FAU speed it up, and on a catchable ball that became the interception. Eric Singleton Jr. did not finish.

Campbell's first series was that same corner in public, a field goal after completions down the field, the start Sumrall told the defensive backs not to get scared of because at corner you get beat and the snap that matters is the one after. Then Vernell Brown III took the half to 45-3, Philo 16-of-21 again for 242 and two, and the field goal was already gone.

A lead like that will eat seven flags after halftime, T.J. Shanahan Jr. wiping a Baugh run and then a personal foul, Roderick Kearney, 1st-and-25, and still feel like a win. Byrum Brown and Jeremiah Cobb will not hide those flags. Sumrall was already taking that to Jordan-Hare when Jadan Baugh went 75 late in the third, 296 yards and five scores in two weeks against a long of 26 a year ago.

He walked off 52-3 unhappy because a guy went the wrong way, the depth behind Baugh was subpar, the line did not give him lanes, and the next backfield is Cobb and Omar Mabson II over 5.5 a carry, Byrum a thousand and 14 last year. Play that second half in conference and they get embarrassed.

Monday, the rooms still had that walk. These games count twice, Sumrall said, overall and conference, and the last two counted once. If he has to get anybody ready, they have the wrong people. He wants sacks and a finish on the quarterback. Singleton and Emmanuel Oyebadejo came out of the boot, limited, questionable, no further than that. Philo has been clean in this building, a chance to win every week if he stays who he has been, and Saturday is the first crowd that will try to take that away.

If the game stays close, Tuesday belonged to Buster Faulkner and Brad White. Faulkner takes a quarterback who has only started here into DJ Durkin's hair-on-fire front plus the noise and said Philo is cool, calm, and collected, and they will coach him through it. White takes a defense that just lived in Gainesville and puts it in Alex Golesh's pace, a nasty line, the fist fight he told them to be ready for.

They have not won in that building since 1999. A close loss this week is how a 7-5 or 8-4 year starts, with Ole Miss, Missouri, South Carolina, Texas, and Georgia in Atlanta still waiting, and 3-0 they have not had since 2019 only if this one never becomes a fight.

Home was the easy part. Saturday is the first night they can lose the close one, and the rest of the year will treat it as the real start.
